findings.text: non-blocking: FIGURE_LINE_RE re-implements the RUBRIC <item>: <verdict> grammar the same module already owns as _PLAN_RUBRIC_LINE_RE at :1794, whose comment states its consumers read one compiled pattern; all six FIGURE_REVIEW_ITEMS names and all seven lines of the stored nova record match the owner's pattern exactly (no leading whitespace, letter-initial names), so this forks a grammar rather than extending it and the two now differ in leading-whitespace and case tolerance.

non-blocking: the precedence rule that an existing item-map entry wins over a verdict line has no test -- the three added cases either omit rubric_items or carry no rubric_lines -- so replacing the blank check with an unconditional `stated[item] = verdict` keeps all 13 tests green while a line could silently overwrite a contradictory recorded verdict.

non-blocking: when the record carries a per-figure `figures` map the `stated` map built from the verdict lines is discarded and the folded per-figure map returned, so a multi-figure record answered in lines is still refused every item; this is latent rather than active -- 9 of 552 stored figure records carry both shapes and 0 of those are incomplete at head.

non-blocking: the new comment narrates the prior defect ("was read as carrying no verdict at all, and a complete review was refused naming every item") where the repository's naming rules ask the mechanism the code enforces, so it should state what the fold guarantees rather than what once went wrong.
